cpu_small-8src.label: on two CPU cores
cpu_small-8src.corpus: 8 datasets, at most 500,000 training rows each (3.5M)
cpu_small-8src.changed: The starting point: the model of normal payments (a VAE) alone. It learns only from legitimate payments and never from a fraud label.

gpu_full-4090.label: on all the data
gpu_full-4090.changed: The same design, 3.4 times larger, on seven times the data. The mean AUROC moved only from 0.829 to 0.833: the fields the model could see, not the number of rows, were the limit.

gpu_full-4090-v4.label: labels, context and the blend
gpu_full-4090-v4.corpus: 9 datasets (AMLworld added), every row (29.2M training rows)
gpu_full-4090-v4.changed: Added decision trees trained on the labelled fraud, facts about the customer's and the merchant's recent history as their inputs, and a blend of the two models with weights for each bank. On the eight datasets v3 had, the mean AUROC rose from 0.833 to 0.907.

v5-h200-e.label: history, entities, supporting models
v5-h200-e.hardware: 1x NVIDIA H200 NVL (rented), 64 CPU cores, 188 GB RAM
v5-h200-e.corpus: 11 datasets (BAF and fraudecom added), every row (30.0M training / 4.3M validation / 8.6M test rows)
v5-h200-e.changed: The VAE now reads the customer's previous 32 payments; new facts about the counterparty, card, device, e-mail domain and address of each payment; two more datasets; six kinds of supporting model. On v4's nine datasets the mean AUROC rose from 0.916 to 0.936.

v5-h200-f.label: one-week fraud labels
v5-h200-f.hardware: the VAE of v5-h200-e; booster side refit on the same rented H200 box
v5-h200-f.changed: Counts the fraud confirmed against each merchant, card and device after a one-week delay as well as after a month, for banks whose labels arrive that fast. The terminal-compromise dataset went from 0.69 to 0.89.

v5-h200-h.label: recent fraud, label delay as a setting
v5-h200-h.hardware: the VAE of v5-h200-e; booster side refit on the same rented H200 box
v5-h200-h.changed: Counts the fraud at each merchant, card and device over the last 7 and 30 days instead of over their whole history, and trains the trees both for banks whose labels take a week and for banks whose labels take a month. 0.963 mean AUROC over the nine shared datasets; shipped until v7.

v6-base-e.label: a pretrained model of payment histories
v6-base-e.hardware: the encoder pretrained on a rented node with 8 NVIDIA B200 GPUs (60,000 steps, 4.5 hours); the VAE of v5-h200-e; booster side refit on the same node
v6-base-e.corpus: the encoder: 16 datasets (the 11 plus five AMLworld variants), 328M training rows, no labels; the booster: the same as v5-h200-e
v6-base-e.changed: Adds a 128-million-parameter model that learnt, from 328 million payments and without fraud labels, to predict a customer's next payment. Its reading of the customer's history goes to the decision trees as 888 extra inputs. One bank gained a lot (86% to 94% of its fraud caught at a 1% false-positive rate) and three lost slightly.

v7-f.label: the history model for two banks
v7-f.hardware: the encoder of v6 and the VAE of v5-h200-e, unchanged; booster side refit on a rented box with 2 NVIDIA H200 NVL GPUs
v7-f.changed: Gives the history model's inputs to the trees for two banks only (TabFormer and the Fraud Detection Handbook simulator), adds a small model trained on fraud labels on top of them, and fits the blend without the VAE. More fraud caught on average at a 1% false-positive rate (86% to 95% on TabFormer), and no bank worse by more than a few millionths of AUROC. The version that ships.
